summary: noelc-css-blender ships obfuscated payload inconsistent with declared CSS utility purpose
details: Package advertises itself as a 'tiny ESM utility for blending CSS custom-property token maps' but index.mjs is a ~306 KB obfuscated file consisting of a base64+XOR(0x98) string array decoded at module load by a dedicated decoder function, padded with thousands of dead-code loops. Decoded entries from the string table include the GitHub bot identity 'dependabot[bot]', the numeric user-id prefix '49699333+' used in dependabot commit author headers, the commit message template 'chore: bump build-cache manifest', the self-reference 'build-cache.mjs', an '/api/v2/...' endpoint fragment, and the AWS SigV4 signing algorithm string 'AWS4-HMAC-SHA256'. None of these are consistent with a CSS token helper. The combined shape — load-time obfuscated decoder, hidden HTTP endpoint reconstruction, AWS SigV4 signing primitives, and dependabot-impersonation commit metadata — matches the loader and self-propagation pattern of maintainer-token-stealing npm worms: on import in an environment holding an npm _authToken or GITHUB_TOKEN, the strings and primitives present are sufficient to sign requests, push commits under a dependabot-looking author identity, and republish into other packages/repos owned by the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
